uncited: Disjoint Set Mesh Optimization is a voxel meshing pipeline that combines voxel-based occlusion culling with plane-wise quad merging to produce a compact triangle mesh from a voxel chunk.
It solves the problem of excessive face count in naive voxel rendering by removing occluded geometry and merging adjacent coplanar quads into larger primitives.

It differs from its parent [Disjoint Set Visible Plane Optimization](4045-disjoint-set-visible-plane-optimization.md) by operating on the full 3D chunk level, adding an initial occlusion culling step before invoking the plane-wise optimizer.
- `DisjointSetVisiblePlaneOptimizer`: An internal component that merges quads on a single 2D plane using a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) structure.
Initialize a `VoxelOcclusionOptimizer` with the input `Chunk<Voxel>`.
Compute the set of visible faces from the chunk using the occluder.
This identifies which voxel faces are not occluded by other solid voxels.
Iterate over each visible plane in the computed visible faces, grouped by axis (X, Y, or Z).
For each plane, run the `DisjointSetVisiblePlaneOptimizer` to merge adjacent quads.
This step uses a Disjoint Set Union data structure to efficiently merge contiguous regions of solid voxels with the same ID into single mesh quads.
Convert the optimized plane data back into a list of `MeshQuad` objects.
Append the resulting quads to the main mesh's quad list.
- Empty chunks or chunks with no solid voxels should return an empty list of quads.
- Precision issues in vertex coordinates may prevent merging of adjacent quads if they are not exactly coplanar.
- Degenerate input (e.g., single voxel) should still produce valid quads.

The general workflow involves building or loading a `Chunk<Voxel>`, using `VoxelOcclusionOptimizer` to determine visible faces, using `DisjointSetVisiblePlaneOptimizer` to merge faces on each plane, and assembling quads into a single optimized mesh.
This workflow is the standard pipeline for this optimization method.
